findings.text: follow-on: the done_when's token clause names this test as passing at head, but it is red in both arms on reckon/ledger.py (reckon/ledger.py: 51666 estimated tokens exceeds the 50000 bound); the node's own touched module reckon/crew_follow_commands.py stands 49486 against the bound, and gate/token-window.log records the run, yet that log is absent from the manifest's test_logs and artifacts lines, so a reader following the manifest cannot reach the only evidence for the clause. ledger.py is unchanged by this node, so this does not hold the node.

item_verdicts.diff: read all three commits 1bc1ee111, 67856d08b and afbabe876 against base ff7ec47c1; the tail lands in reckon/crew/needs_you.py:241 as drain_tail, the follower gains only the call at reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:1127-1130, and tests/test_follow_drain_line.py, tests/test_a_pane_does_not_settle_during_admission.py and the landing fragment account for the rest, all inside the declared write paths.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when's behavioural clauses are asserted by tests/test_follow_drain_line.py (one drain whose tail names one run needing the coordinator at :302, the peer session's run absent at :307, the second drain reading fleet drained at :324) and by tests/test_a_pane_does_not_settle_during_admission.py:340; the negative control withheld the tail and the first case failed at :302 with EXIT=1.
item_verdicts.goal: the goal is for the follower's settle row to carry a tail saying the session's fleet is drained or how many runs need the coordinator, counted by reckon/crew/needs_you.py; reckon/crew/needs_you.py:241 composes that tail from needs_you_runs and reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:1108 appends it after the row's existing prefix.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it states the two arms by their own logs (base 4 failed 570 passed, head 4 failed 571 passed, the same four ids), the negative control and its red line, the measurement module and cwd, and files the pre-existing ledger.py token-window failure as a follow-on.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the manifest's six declared paths; the diff touches four of them plus the landing fragment, and every changed path is inside the declaration.

justifications.durability: gate/negative-control.log withholds the tail from the settle row and reddens tests/test_follow_drain_line.py::test_a_drain_names_the_run_that_needs_you at :302 with EXIT=1 ('the drained pane names no run that needs the coordinator'), so the added assertion fails on the exact regression it guards and is not a value compared against itself.
justifications.evidence: the done_when's command is the manifest's tests line and its result is recorded at gate/head-arm.log (4 failed, 571 passed, EXIT=1) against gate/base-arm.log (4 failed, 570 passed, EXIT=1), with the same four pre-existing ids in both arms, so added_failure_count 0 is derived from the logs rather than claimed.
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/needs_you.py:236 names the drained word as a module constant in the file's constant style, the module follows the surrounding docstring voice at :241, and the inline import at reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:1120 matches _follower_end_event's own inline-import idiom at :1073.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/needs_you.py:241 returns DRAINED_TAIL, '1 run needs the coordinator', or an N-run count from needs_you_runs, and reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:1108 appends it after the untouched 'no live work in {session} since {stamp}' prefix the plan requires.
justifications.reuse: the tail is defined in the owning module reckon/crew/needs_you.py:241 and composes that module's own needs_you_runs, so it extends the owner rather than forking it; a search of reckon/ for an existing count-to-phrase composer found only reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:1042 which names run ids for the end row, a different row and wording the plan prescribes.
justifications.scope_discipline: every changed path in the diff sits inside the manifest's declared write paths, and the docs/figures path declared but unused is a declared path, not an extra one.
